story: A Completely Non-Technical Explanation of Deep Learning
text: If anyone is looking for a quick overview of how LLMs are built, I highly recommend this video by Steve Seitz: [VIDEO] . It does an excellent job of taking you from 0 to a decent understanding without dumbing down the content or abusing analogies.

Consider the following frame/time from the video: [VIDEO] At this point in time in the video, we see the following 3 things: 1) Fourier Series 2) Taylor Series 3) Neural Network The remainder of the video goes on to show how Neural Networks can approximate functions -- much like the Fourier Series and Taylor Series can... Now, I don't hold an advanced Ph.D. degree in Math, and prior to watching this video, I had never made the connection between Fourier Series, Taylor Series, and Neural Networks... I knew about each of those independently -- but prior to watching the video, I never made the connection that they can be used to approximate one another. And that's the one of the key words -- approximate . The other key word is Identity -- as in Mathematical Identity ... That's because IF two Mathematical Objects (functions, algorithms, call them what-you-will) are approximately equal -- then there should be a set of conditions (i.e., "If and only if...", etc.), a set of rigorously defined mathematical constraints which, if those conditions/constraints are met, then the two Mathematical Objects are exactly precisely equivalent -- under those rigorously defined conditions/constraints.... In other words, under those rigorously defined conditions/constraints -- one Mathematical Object could be substituted for another -- with no loss of precision or result.
